checks.label: dead-or-leftover-code
checks.name: Dead or leftover code in the diff: commented-out code, #if 0 blocks, unused includes/aliases/constants/functions/fields, unreachable branches, always-empty parameters
checks.description: Trigger: an added line is code behind // or #if 0; an added #include, using-alias, constant, function, member or parameter has no consumer at HEAD (grep h/ src/ t/ for the identifier); a new parameter is passed a constant empty value at every call site; an if/else branch repeats the initialization above it or sits under an enclosing guard that fixes its condition; a statement follows TRON_ASSERT(false); a loop header became a bare block but the body still prepares the next iteration; a duplicate TRACE_EVENT_END or similar remains after an edit. Question: which line at HEAD compiles, calls or reads this, and if none, why is it in the PR instead of deleted. Wade's wording is a short question ('can this go away?', 'don't need this bf16.hpp include now right?', 'still need this log?'). Rows 2737826254, 2737844615, 2737943442, 2737956124, 2737956568, 2738033592 and 3350291154 were tagged 10-partial by the classifier: check 10 asks whether a hunk belongs to the feature; this check widens it to lines that belong to no feature (development residue). 3307473806 (usleep commented out, a behavior change) is placed here by its trigger (commented-out code line) and should be answered with the behavior question. 3405963004 is Wade's self-correction that found a dead else branch.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: grep for consumers of every added identifier and include at HEAD; detect // code and #if 0 lines syntactically; detect constant-empty arguments at all call sites

checks.label: typos-in-comments-docs-strings
checks.name: Spelling and surface text defects in added comments, doc lines, assert messages and markdown (plus over-wide markdown lines)
checks.description: Trigger: an added comment line, doc line, or string literal contains a misspelled or run-together English word, a lowercase sentence start, a heading whose case differs from siblings, or a name of a macro that does not exist (LOG_TOKEN_TIMS); an added .md line is far wider than the file's wrap width (3778051701, 3778058064: 144 and 130 columns in files wrapped near 90). Question: does the added line read as correct English, and does every identifier-shaped token in it exist. Wade answers almost always with a ```suggestion block carrying the corrected line and no prose (3307296300, 3307297422, 3307298245, 3307366165, 3307465363 are five consecutive one-line fixes on one file). He fixes pre-existing typos when re-indentation puts them in the diff (3307465363) and asks for a typo fix while commenting on something else (3973917755, in check 10).
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: spell-check added comment/doc/string tokens against a dictionary plus the repository identifier set; measure .md line widths against the file's median

checks.label: magic-numbers-and-constant-names
checks.name: Bare literals in production code need a name; named constants must not be replaced by literals; constant names carry a role, not a value
checks.description: Existing check 13 fires only on value-suffixed constant families (5420005787 row 1, 6021333114). The 16 other rows show Wade's broader and far more frequent trigger: any bare integer literal other than 0/1 in production arithmetic, index, stride, mask, capacity or size (2620219338 '(4, 8, 32, 128 etc)', 2915246595 '2048 is a bit cryptic', 2636393495 1024*1024, 2897210663 k_tmp[4][8]); a removed named constant whose added twin is a literal or sizeof (2915275194 hwkv_max_layers -> 32, 2948209837 POS_DATA_SIZE -> sizeof(bf16), 3307459854 timeout_ns -> 1000); a literal that duplicates a reachable named constant (2948416014 128 vs hwkv_tok_per_page, 2737603648 layer == 0 vs LAYER_IDX_FOR_DEBUG, 2789750267 31 vs max_num_fetchers - 1); a capacity literal with no provenance (3120756577 reserve(64), 3350173837 ring size 2048); a literal that gates debug output (2915186372 tok_ix > 4000); a count constant reused as an error sentinel (3235796275 NUM_CLASSES); an unexplained / 2 (3454926024). Question: can a reader at this line say what the literal measures, does a named constant with that meaning already exist in reachable headers, and why did a name become a literal. Trigger of check 13 must widen from 'value-suffixed family' to 'any production literal without a role name, any constant-to-literal replacement, any literal duplicating an existing constant'. Severity ranges from 'nit' to normal; he files repeat offenders as a clean-up to-do (2636393495, 2620219338) and asks for one common location (2620219338, 2947931435 in declaration hygiene).
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for literal detection, constant-to-literal replacement and duplicate-of-existing-constant (grep headers for the value and meaning); needs_domain to name what a hardware literal means

checks.label: debug-and-log-hygiene
checks.name: Debug switches, dumps and log lines: not left enabled, behind the file's existing guard or macro, through the right category, consistent with siblings
checks.description: Trigger: a diff turns '// #define DEBUG_*' (or LOG_*, MORE_*_DEBUG) into an active define, or adds an active debug define, in a header or production .cpp (2789808472, 3124878965, 2759894229, 2759903853); an added debug dump or spdlog::debug sits unguarded while the file guards sibling calls with a compile-time macro or a dbg_*_log macro (2719160746, 2719161128, 2737832765); a new log call uses an older sibling category macro when the diff itself introduced one for this category (3405973171, 3405974281); a log line carries a developer tag or looks like a leftover trace (3002085391 'MRC allocated shard'); two log lines have identical format text for different variables (3002066935); a variable is declared outside the #ifdef block that is its only user (2915258232); a block of debug helpers clutters the production header (2948027543); a test prints a result unconditionally where siblings print only on mismatch (2620236334); a TRACE_EVENT moves from a detail category to the default one or is added on a per-request path (3456320516, Perfetto buffer overflow). Question: is this debug switch meant to ship enabled, does any PR text say so, and does the added output go through the guard and category the file already uses. Wade words these as 'intend to leave this enabled?', 'wrap in `#ifdef WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS`?', 'still need this log?'. Rows 2789808472 and 3456320516 were tagged 10-partial by the classifier (an unstated change); kept here by mechanism.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: diff lines that activate a *_DEBUG/LOG_* define, unguarded dump calls next to a file-level guard macro, log calls not using the file's newest category macro, identical format strings

checks.label: control-flow-and-value-invariants
checks.name: Every branch, exit and configuration keeps the invariant: counts after early exit, out-values on every branch, loop bounds at boundaries, init, alignment, NaN handling, flag sense, device index, model-shape assumptions
checks.description: Trigger: a pre-computed count survives a loop break (2983833171); a loop bound derived from a rounded-down index includes an empty block at an exact boundary (3002297607); a helper's out-value is assigned in only one of several loops (3437517809); a refactor drops std::isnan/isinf handling before a tolerance compare (2771743559); a reference into a std::vector is held across push_back (3120788282); a one-character flip of a default's comparison sense inverts a documented macro (3463061252); a stack buffer without alignas is handed to an aligned SIMD store (3960506641); an index expression changes with no comment (2948176586 '.i' -> token_positions, 'were we grabbing the (potentially) wrong token-id all this time?'); a local aggregate is declared without an initializer (2789725609, 2789768975); a per-device container is indexed with literal 0 on a path that runs under TP2/TP4 (3029339639); an allocation constant silently fixes a model parameter (2947992404 8192 assumes 8 kv_heads); a timeout is lowered while runtime logs already show values past it (3236579299); a test swaps a resource accessor without saying it is the same queue (2737853978); a subsystem is called unconditionally while its configure is gated (2948090978). Question: name the input (boundary token, zero-iteration path, second device, other build, larger model) on which old and new code differ, and show the PR says so. Several rows endorse a Cursor/Claude/GPT finding after Wade's own reading (2983833171, 3002297607, 3437517809, 3463061252, 2948090978); 3002297607 asks for 'a quick diag test' when reading cannot settle it.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for most (count-after-break, sentinel-not-set, isnan dropped, reference-across-push_back, literal device index, flag-sense flip, missing alignas vs aligned store); needs_runtime for boundary off-by-one and observed timeout values; needs_domain for model-shape constants

checks.label: one-definition-reuse-existing
checks.name: One definition: reuse the existing helper, value, local or loop instead of a second copy that can drift
checks.description: Trigger: a hand-written loop or predicate reproduces an existing helper (2719158416 mwaitx::wait_for_not_event, 3029194687 fwd_hw_attn_enabled(), 3454460758 duplicated getenv across a layer boundary, 3102140611 resize); a value is re-derived from a formula or literal where the model or config already holds it (2897190682 pre_attn scalar 1.0f, 3036995239 1/sqrt(head_size) vs the state constructor's gemma branch); the same key or constant is spelled two ways (4147010638 pool_worker inline vs helper, 3350031805 message literal 32 vs max_cmd_fifo_depth 1024); a safety-critical statement sequence or struct is copied (3907214892 four copies of reservation.commit() -> guard.commit() -> tracker.push); a zero-arg accessor is re-called when a local holds it (3029340601); a lambda only forwards to a function with the identical signature (2954613896); two adjacent loops walk the same container (4029533521); an if/else repeats one statement with one token changed (3405150087); a per-element cast could be one pointer cast (2700506675). Question: does a definition of this helper, value or key already exist at BASE or in this diff, and if the convention changes at one copy, does the compiler or a test catch the other. Wade words these as 'couldn't we use X for this?', 'this should be replaced with the X function I just added early this week', 'Suggest one helper for all three'.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: grep for an existing helper by shape (busy-wait, getenv name, predicate), for other spellings of the same value/key in the subsystem, and for near-verbatim copies of a block in the diff

checks.label: declaration-hygiene-and-placement
checks.name: Declaration choices: unsigned for never-negative quantities, const for fixed globals, no member derivable from a sibling, explicit member initializers, redundant specifiers, include style, constants and declarations in the right place, oversized functions
checks.description: Trigger: a count/size/index local or parameter is int or int64_t (3430026641, 3437522787, 3437526764, 3437527579: 'Wouldn't `uint` make more sense'); a file-scope UPPER_CASE variable lacks const (2380221355); a struct holds both a count and a container, or an index plus a pointer that carries it (3010846319, 2913598312); a struct gains default member initializers inconsistently or redundantly (2941290531, 4125818552 cites the C++ value-initialization rule); 'public:' first in a struct (3391446464); a third-party header included with quotes and separated from its siblings (3405979630); constexpr definitions buried mid-file (2947931435 'move all these constexpr to the top'); a function already hundreds of lines long grows on both branches (3405172585 'pull these stanzas into helper utilities'). Question: does the type, qualifier, placement and layout match what the quantity is and what the file already does, and does the repository state a rule (he asks twice whether an 'official guideline' exists: 2789768975 in invariants, 2941290531 here). Severity: nit or 'next iteration'; 4125818552 and 2941290531 are approvals that still state the preference.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: signed types on count-named variables vs unsigned callers, non-const uppercase globals, count+container pairs, first access specifier equal to default, quoted third-party includes, constexpr position in file, function length delta

checks.label: fail-loud-bound-every-wait
checks.name: Fail loud: assert instead of silently continuing, clamping or dropping; bound every spin-wait; check every count against its capacity; print the offending value
checks.description: Trigger: a sentinel branch on a value feeding a hardware command logs or skips instead of asserting (2983787051 'We can't meaningfully continue on with this right?'); a runtime count from a vector is copied into a fixed-size array (MAX_B) with no bound check at any writer (2982760463, 3002034511); a range guard returns early 'for the tests' so production drops counts silently (4125033677 'Prefer asserting'); std::min clamps a model parameter on a path an upstream screen makes unreachable (3866435051); a self-move guard or 'defensive' wait exists for a state that cannot happen (2825119397, 3307359535 'defensive/sanity guarding?'); a while loop polls a flag with no timeout and no debug_exit (3307412051, 3342904643 'It turns a loud tripwire into a silent forever-hang.'); an assert message omits the variable it tests (2670489106). Question: if this condition is reached, is every outcome wrong, and does the code then abort with the value named, or hang or miscount silently. He asks whether the guard is defensive or expected before asking for the assert, and marks unbounded spins 'probably a next iteration/enhancement effort'.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: find vector.size() -> fixed array copies without a bound assert, early returns with 'test' in the comment, std::min on model params, pause-only loops without deadline, asserts whose message lacks the tested variable

checks.label: passages-a-reader-cannot-use
checks.name: Text a GitHub reader two years later cannot use: PR-body noise, stale body after review rounds, code comments citing review rounds, Story numbers, local paths, feature-narrating Notes, design-time musings
checks.description: Existing check 9 covers the PR body (5420005787 row 6 'Assertion-count arithmetic, UTC build timestamps and log paths can go.'). The other 8 rows widen it to code comments and to the body's currency: a comment cites 'PR 4596 review round 4' (4146947611 'probably don't want to reference ... like this', 4146959502 'Scrub please.'); a comment cites 'Story 2814' (3350285744 'don't mention Story numbers in comments'); a comment points to for_claude/heap-profile.log (3227565141); a 13-line Note narrates a bug fix (3866668853 'not worthy of it's own noisy Note'); a comment ties a general trace event to the feature Note (3350412400); a comment still asks a design question the PR answers (2789661703); the PR body no longer matches the code after review rounds (5371062950 'your PR description is stale at this point'). Trigger must widen from 'Status/Verification sections of the body' to every added comment line matching review|round|Story|ticket|PR #|a path outside the repo, every Note longer than ~6 lines that restates a fix, and a body whose last edit predates review-driven commits. Question: would deleting this clause change any decision about the head, and does it explain the code by a lasting reason.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: grep added comments for review/round/Story/ticket/PR numbers and non-repo paths; measure Note length vs content; compare body edit time with commit dates

checks.label: concurrency-and-async-completion
checks.name: Concurrency and asynchronous completion: a wait after a per-device loop covers every device, a racy getter is read once, a reader waits for every writer of shared storage, a buffer outlives its DMA, locks live with the state they protect, atomics match the cross-thread set
checks.description: Trigger: a completion wait after a loop that issued one async operation per device takes get_device(0) (2789792758, 2789796269 'we'll be waiting on the first device's xfer'); a getter named as racy (count_complete_gofs) is called in the guard and again in the computation (3125517302); a readiness predicate is narrowed while the consumer reads at page granularity (3970590653, blocking, 'allows attention to read unfinished V data'); an in-flight DMA record can be dropped without abandon() (5498556672); a lock_guard spans a whole loop (2983867856 'because you don't want someone to update the tree during your search/gather?'); some members of a group are std::atomic (3406007619 'I assume these reuse counters (and only these counters) are atomics because the FUSE reader ... is a different thread?'); new parallelism reaches a per-device queue without a lock (3275212298); a mutex is added at the call site in another file rather than in PosDevice/DmaQueue, spans a busy-wait, and serializes parallel callers (3277240111). Question: which thread reads and writes each touched object, does every issued operation get waited on, and does the lock sit with the state, cover only the mutation, and get taken on every mutating path. He states the thread model back to the author as a question before asking for a change.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for fixed-index wait after per-device loop, double call of a racy getter, lock placement outside the owning file, atomic/plain mix; needs_domain for narrowed readiness predicates and DMA lifetime

checks.label: comment-matches-code
checks.name: A comment or doc sentence matches the code it sits on and has exactly one reading
checks.description: Trigger: a comment names an identifier other than the one the code below reads (3307483528 prep_done vs hw_prepared, 3437533506 ares_fields vs wres_fields); a comment states a runtime string the implementation does not produce (3405930260 <bdf> vs dev->idx, 'I suspect this got copied from other (inaccurate) fuse-related comments'); a comment describes in present tense an algorithm the diff removed (3120684367); a notation contradicts the comment's own text (3356922988 'Q3.61 right? Not Q.61?'); a negated parenthetical reads as the opposite precondition (2828677364 '(no shuffle)' vs pre-shuffled); an elided clause reads two ways (4095187050 'excepted' vs accepted); a trailing comment restates the identifier (3002013791). Question: for every identifier, literal, tense and negation in the added comment, does the code or the rest of the comment agree, and can a first-time reader expand it into one sentence. Mostly suggestion blocks with the corrected line plus '... right?'.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: cross-check identifiers named in a comment against the statements it heads, literal paths/format strings against the implementation, tense against removed lines; needs_domain for notation and ambiguity

checks.label: unrelated-or-unexplained-hunks
checks.name: Hunks the feature does not need or the body does not explain: merge artifacts, deleted placeholder files, removed comments with external consumers, content with no origin in any source branch, added build flags with unexplained provenance
checks.description: Existing check 10 covers 5420005787 row 2 (AMX tile constants and the t_heap_v2 check 'aren't part of typed tensors; please split them out'). The other rows widen the trigger: duplicated #include lines after a merge (2915281512 'perhaps a merge artifact?', 2915281835); deletion of stats/.gitkeep in a one-file fix (3197414598 'was this intentional?'); removal of a 'DO NOT RENAME as packaging is dependent' comment (3973917755); a volatile qualifier on 19 members present in neither source branch of a merge PR (2629374536 'So where is this coming from?'); new -mavx/-mavx2 flags on a library that built without them (2670498736). Question: does any body sentence or commit subject account for this hunk, does it exist on a branch the PR claims to merge from, and does the removed line protect a consumer outside the file. Trigger must widen from 'hunks with no PR identifier' to 'any added line that already exists in the file, any deleted or added file no sentence names, any removed comment naming an external consumer, and in a merge/sync PR any content absent from both parents'.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: duplicate-line detection at HEAD, file add/delete vs body text, removed comment lines with consumer words, diff of a merge PR against both parents

checks.label: identifier-names-its-role
checks.name: An identifier says what it holds or does, in the code base's own spelling
checks.description: Trigger: a member or variable named by a bare generic noun or letter (2982403509 'layers' -> kv_shard_layers, 3075717295 tok_ix_per_b whose comment says per-Q, 2842854014 firstcheck next to first); two-letter parameter abbreviations where the code base spells n_kv_heads/head_size (2897235803); a name that states a phase or behavior the call does not have (3001991780 prepare_ inside launch_, 3769684790 which half of a traced/untraced split keeps the original name); a new user-facing name whose casing differs from its siblings (3580238651 'Benchmark only' vs lower-case benchmark labels). Question: would a reader at a use site know from the identifier alone what it holds, and does it follow the dominant spelling. Related: check 13's constant stems; function-name-vs-behavior rows went to the test-name check (2380263378).
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: generic-noun and single-letter member names, abbreviation parameters vs dominant repo spelling, phase words in nested call names, casing of new label strings vs existing ones

checks.label: document-the-new-thing
checks.name: A new parameter, helper, routine, default or term gets a comment or definition at its declaration
checks.description: Trigger: a new defaulted parameter with no comment and a hedge word in its name (2948108341 'can we document `kv_hint` (e.g. why is it a hint)'); a header function whose only callers are tests, or a parameter production always passes as one constant (3866568650, 3866590750 'this `xfer_k_entry` is a UT-only utility function. We should document that clearly'); a new routine or env var read with no comment (3036997452 'I'm a fan of comments'); defaults visible only at the declaration (2789826297, pushed back: C++ forbids repeating them); a specialist term or mode name used before definition (4095287201 'erased'?, 3855274893 'first mention of safe mode'). Question: could a reader of this file alone learn what the item is for, who calls it, and what its default means. Severity nit to minor; always an ask, never a block.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: new parameters/functions without a leading comment, header functions whose callers are all under t/, getenv names without a comment, first-use terms with no definition in the file

checks.label: tests-exist-run-and-reach-production-path
checks.name: A test exists for the new primitive, runs at this head (including hardware-labelled ones CI cannot run), goes through the production entry point, mirrors a changed production formula, and cleans its artifacts
checks.description: Trigger: a new reusable primitive lands with no file under t/ naming it (4614385493 'Are you going to build a unit-test for this? ... verifying multi-producer ordering, wrap-around, etc'); the body's test plan lists only static checks on hardware-facing constants (4265644124 'please run at least a subset of representative UTs'); a bot raises a double-visit finding and no multi-user run is cited (3156090573); the CI lane cannot execute FPGA-labelled tests so the reviewer runs the whole suite himself and pastes the ctest summary (4131374395); new tests call the wrapped function while the orchestration the diff changed is never entered (3960538961 'The added tests call `shard::xfer_gofs` directly'); a production formula changes while tests assign the same field (2771720147 'this should be updated in the t_hwattention / t_hwattention_replay tests as well'); a test writes /tmp and for_agent files and reads the same pattern back (2737978696). Question: which test reaches the changed code through its production caller at this head, which assertion fails if it is wrong, and is there evidence the run happened. Distinct from check 3 (a test that exists but silently skips) and check 4 (two tests on one call).
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for existence (grep t/ for the new symbol), production-path reachability (call graph from the test to the changed function) and formula mirroring (grep tests for the assigned field); needs_runtime for running the hardware-labelled suite

checks.label: design-granularity-ownership-placement
checks.name: Design questions: one owner per record, a key stable across forwards, classification at the granularity production batching needs, declarations in the header that owns the subsystem
checks.description: Trigger: one logical record written from two layers (4125033653 'Any other caller of state.forward(...) gives forwards == 0 next to nonzero token_jobs'); a per-worker table sized by one count and indexed by another that a per-forward decision can change (4125033686); a whole-forward classification validated only under runtron while rinzler batches are mixed (4125033664 'The runtron validation can't show this'); a declaration in a header about another subsystem (3405003751 'odd place to declare this', 2760690084 float helpers in bf16.hpp); a design proposal in prose whose assumption needs restating (2699944590 'assume at most one wrap'); a review-round change that moved a definition out of the diff instead of adding the asked one-line extern (3463077403 'This isn't quite what I meant'). Question: can any caller reach one writer without the other, does the same index mean the same thread every time, does the bucket match the production case, and does the receiving header own the symbol. Wade poses these as a question with two alternatives ('was keying by attention index deliberate, or key by pool worker index ... or record n_attn_workers per forward').
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for two-writer records, size-vs-index mismatch and header-topic mismatch; needs_domain for production batching behavior and design intent

checks.label: claim-wider-than-code
checks.name: A sentence in the body, a Note, a comment or a spec promises more subjects or paths than the code enforces or measures
checks.description: Existing check 6 covers the compile-time guarantee case (4188336267 'a bare pointer is a compile error holds for V only'). The other rows widen the subject: a timer documented with an 'or' over two paths is measured on one (4125033634 'That spin is never timed. So on a CPU-attention run join_wait_cycles reads 0'); the body attributes a runtron option to Perfetto (5106398334 part 1); a comment says a function is 'called between forward passes' and nothing calls it (3029165954 'how come I don't see this being called anywhere?'); the spec says 'one or more chunks' while heap_start reads chunks[0] (3227529208 'So is the spec wrong? Or are these functions insufficient?'); the file header says 'default ON' while the #ifndef fallback still says 0 (3501641254). Trigger must widen from 'compile-time rejection sentence' to any sentence whose subject is plural, an 'or', 'every', 'between passes', a default, or a component name. Question: for every subject the sentence covers, which code line reaches it, and does the sentence say so. Both repairs are offered: change the code, or narrow the text.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: extract plural/or/every subjects from body, Note and comment sentences and trace each to a code path; grep for callers of functions whose comment names a lifecycle point

checks.label: test-silently-skips-or-cannot-fail
checks.name: A test that exists but does not run or cannot fail: hidden Catch2 tag, bare return above assertions, hardware-probe early return, a fake that discards the output, the opposite build configuration never run
checks.description: Existing check 3 covers the available() gate (4188336256). Four more rows share the mechanism: a tag changed to '[.name]' hides the test by default (2790161683 'did you intend to disable this test?'); a bare `return;` added above the REQUIREs (2737861302 'did you intend to leave this `return`?'); pos_fake::xfer_n_blocks discards every descriptor argument so wrong HBM bases pass (3960538177 'incorrect HBM bases, fetchers, source offsets, or transfer lengths would still pass'); the change sits under #ifdef FWD_HW_RESULTS and the other configuration was not sanity-tested (2915270383). Trigger must widen from 'hardware probe before a formula assertion' to 'any exit, hidden tag, stub or build gate between the TEST_CASE start and the assertion, and any sibling configuration of a changed #ifdef region'. Question: if the production code emitted the wrong value, which assertion fails on the gating lane, and in which configurations.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: Catch2 tag starting with '.', unconditional return/SKIP above assertions, fake methods with unused parameters on the call path, #ifdef/#else siblings of changed regions vs the body's test configurations

checks.label: branch-state-at-every-push
checks.name: Branch state at every push: squash fixup clusters, rebase onto main, stale copies of another branch, in-flight conflicts, earlier suggestions applied
checks.description: Existing check 11 covers the squash ask (5420005787 row 3 'Commits: 20, three of them rewording one Note. Please squash.'). The other rows show that Wade re-reads the branch state at each push and at approval: 'Also needs rebased.' (4373886636); a ported header is an old snapshot of hwattention_sync (3206111074 'Be sure you are rebased to latest'); a heads-up that his own local work deletes the function the hunk touches (2728371157); a suggestion from the previous round still unapplied after a new push (3002050036 'looks like this still needs fixed'). Trigger must widen from 'fixup clusters' to mergeability (gh pr view --json mergeable), freshness of copied files against their source branch, and the resolution state of earlier suggestion blocks at the new head. Question: is the branch mergeable as it stands, does every copied file match its source at its current head, and is every earlier suggestion either applied or answered.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: gh mergeable state, diff of ported files against the named source branch, unresolved suggestion threads whose original line still exists at HEAD; needs_domain for conflicts with unpushed local work

This is the opposite direction of check 13 (which only asks whether a value-suffixed name has a role).

checks.label: redundant-code-simplify
checks.name: A statement, member, branch or scope adds nothing the surrounding code or the language does not already give
checks.description: What breaks: readability only. A lambda forwards all arguments to a function with the identical std::function signature; a hand-written push_back loop next to a sibling resize (Wade withdrew this one after checking the element type); a per-element cast where one pointer cast outside the loop suffices; a call that re-iterates the list the loop above just filled; a second pos_list_devices() call where the local devs exists; an else branch that re-assigns the initial values; 'public:' as the first specifier of a struct; a memset and braces left from a loop that became a block; nshards next to shards.size(); device_idx next to dev->idx; explicit = 0 initializers that value-initialization already gives. Procedure: for each added statement ask whether removing it changes any observable state; compare added members with fields reachable from sibling members; compare added loops with calls or loops on the same container in the same function; compare added initializers with the language rule for the construction path. Severity is always nit or pedantic (Wade says 'pedantic' 5 times in 267 texts, computed); he phrases them as questions and accepts pushback.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: local reading of the hunk and the enclosing function; low cost, low severity; report as nits only.

checks.label: duplicate-logic-use-existing-helper
checks.name: New code re-derives a value, predicate, sequence or helper that already exists elsewhere in the repository
checks.description: What breaks: two copies drift. A hand-written spin loop duplicates mwaitx::wait_for_not_event; an inline getenv/device test duplicates fwd_hw_attn_enabled(); a second getenv of USE_HW_ATTN across the pos/tron layer boundary; a pool-worker key computed inline at one site and by stats->pool_worker() at two others; an if/else whose branches are the same stanza except a type name; the safety-critical reservation.commit() -> guard.commit() -> tracker.push() sequence copied four times across gof.cpp and model.hpp; log calls using the old dbg_hwattn_cmds_log where the same diff defined dbg_wlr_log; gof_configure passed 1.0f where the model holds the real pre-attention scalar; 1/sqrt(head_size) re-derived while the state constructor already handles gemma softcapping. Procedure: for every added predicate, formula, wait loop or sequence, grep h/ and src/ for a function or expression with the same operands; for every helper or macro the diff itself introduces, list added call sites in the same subsystem that use an older sibling instead; for any value passed as a literal to a configure function, find the member that already computes it; for any sequence whose comment says ordering matters, count its copies at HEAD.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: grep for same-operand expressions and for the diff's own new helpers; the layering constraint (3454460758) needs the include-layer rule from docs.

checks.label: identifier-name-states-role
checks.name: An identifier does not say what it holds, contradicts its own comment or behavior, or breaks the surrounding convention
checks.description: What breaks: a reader at the use site cannot tell what the thing is. 'layers' for per-layer K/V HBM bases; tok_ix_per_b whose own comment says per-Q; 'firstcheck' next to an existing 'first'; nk/nh/hs where the code base spells n_kv_heads; prepare_hardware_attn_job calling hw_prepare inside launch_hw_attention; a function named 'indefinitely' that times out after 4 billion cycles; a wrapper split that keeps the old name on the new wrapper (Wade withdrew after seeing the transparent-inheritance reason); a GitHub label 'Benchmark only' beside lower-case 'benchmark' labels; value-suffixed constants whose stem carries no role (5420005787 part; see pr-body-and-branch-state) and a mask spelled V_ODD_TOKEN_LANE_MASK_0XFFFF0000 in v_vnni.hpp while its partner kv_cache.hpp spells the same mask as the local hi_16_of_32 (6021333114). Procedure: for every added or renamed identifier compare the name with its trailing comment, with the sibling names in the same scope, with the dominant spelling of the same quantity in the repository and with what the body does; for names that state a phase or behavior (prepare, launch, indefinitely, traced) check the body honors it. Check 13 covers only value-suffixed constant families; this widens to members, parameters, flags, functions and labels.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: name-vs-comment and name-vs-sibling comparisons are mechanical; whether 'indefinitely' is misleading (2380263378) needs the mwaitx operand semantics.

checks.label: missing-explanation-at-declaration
checks.name: A new parameter, helper, term, clause or default lands with no explanation a reader can use
checks.description: What breaks: a reader of the file alone cannot learn what the thing is for. kv_hint = nullptr with no comment and a hedge word in the name; xfer_k_entry is a unit-test-only utility and purposely forwards head_size, undocumented; a 20-line device_thread routine and the TRON_POISON_BITS env var with no comment; 'erased' and 'safe mode' used in a spec without definition or pointer; '(C2C egress excepted)' readable two ways; default argument values visible only in the header (Wade asks for a comment at the definition since C++ forbids repeating them); older specs demoted to 'no longer the authority' with no retirement plan. Procedure: for every added signature parameter, env-var read, function over about 20 lines, and quoted or capitalized term in prose, require a definition at first use or a pointer; for defaults moved to a header, suggest a comment at the definition; for 'superseded' wording ask who removes the old document and when. This matches the plain-English rule 'define a term at first use' applied to code and specs.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: detect undocumented new parameters, env reads, long functions and first-use terms; whether a hedge word is justified needs reading the body.

checks.label: index-count-or-early-exit-mismatch
checks.name: A count, bound or wait does not match the set it is supposed to cover
checks.description: What breaks: memory or hardware state. nshards copied from vector.size() into a MAX_B-sized array with no bound check at two write sites; num_wcmds pre-computed from the full input while a break leaves slots uninitialized; a loop bound `<= (tok_ix / shard_tokens) * shard_tokens` includes the freshly allocated empty shard at an exact boundary; write_tx_descriptors returns its sentinel first_desc for legacy requests (set only inside the metadata loop); wait_for_xfer_blocks on get_device(0) after a loop that issued one DMA per device (two sites); (*pos_list_devices())[0] on a path that runs under TP2/TP4. Procedure: for every runtime count that indexes a fixed-capacity array find a statement on every path that proves count <= capacity; for every pre-computed count read after a loop with break, check it is reset to the number filled; for every out-value initialized to a sentinel list the branches that assign it; for every wait/join after a per-device loop check it iterates the same set; for every literal index into a per-device container ask what selects the device under multi-device configurations. Wade relays bot or Claude findings here and endorses them ('I do think there's merit', 'Cursorbot's observation seems valid'), and asks for a diagnostic test when reading cannot settle it.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for bound checks, sentinel-return branches and fixed-index waits after loops; the exact-boundary off-by-one (3002297607) needs a runtime diagnostic, which Wade himself asked for.

checks.label: silent-fallback-where-assert-belongs
checks.name: Code clamps, skips, spins or returns silently on a state that should abort loudly
checks.description: What breaks: a defect is hidden instead of caught. std::min of n_kv_heads against HW_MAX_KV_HEADS on a path the shape screen already makes unreachable; hook range guards that return early so wrong indices go uncounted in production (and row() already asserts the same bounds); `if (this != &other)` in a move assignment where self-move is never intended; a shard_stride == 0 branch that continues building a device command; a prep_done wait whose comment does not say whether the state occurs normally; an unbounded spin on in_flight that replaces a TRON_ASSERT and duplicates rxinfo_ring backpressure; ck_pr_stall loops with no bound and no way to reach debug_exit; an assert message that omits the offending head_size. Procedure: for every added clamp, early return, sentinel branch or spin loop ask whether a bug-free caller can reach the condition; if not, propose TRON_ASSERT or debug_exit; for every added wait loop require a bound or timeout that ends in a diagnosed exit; for every assertion on a runtime variable require the value in the message. Ask form: should we just assert this?, we can't meaningfully continue on with this right?, It turns a loud tripwire into a silent forever-hang.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: find added guards and spin loops and trace whether an upstream screen already excludes the condition; the root-cause masking claim (3342904643) needs hardware and runtime knowledge.

checks.label: type-and-initialization-choice
checks.name: Signed type for a never-negative quantity, uninitialized aggregate local, mutable global constant, or inconsistent member initialization
checks.description: What breaks: implicit conversions and undefined reads. expected_blocks, res_per_block, res_bytes_per_block, pad_bytes declared int/int64_t while never negative and while callers pass uint64_t (four comments, three as suggestion blocks); dma_xfer_state locals with no initializer (Wade suggested = {0}, then conceded the struct has default member initializers); file-scope MWAIT_C0 as mutable uint32_t; praise for default member initializers followed by the question what the project standard is. Procedure: for every added local, parameter or member whose name denotes a count, size, index or byte length, check the type is unsigned and matches every caller's type; for every added aggregate local without an initializer, read the struct for default member initializers before suggesting = {}; for every file-scope UPPER_CASE variable require const/constexpr unless written later. Note the repeated question about an official initialization guideline (2789768975, 2941290531): the C++ guide answer belongs in the skill prose.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: name-pattern plus type scan of added declarations, caller type comparison, struct default-initializer lookup; fully static.

checks.label: disabled-code-left-in
checks.name: Commented-out statements or #if 0 blocks added or kept in the diff
checks.description: What breaks: dead text that a reader must parse and that may hide a disabled check. `// k_xfers_completed = 0;` duplicated in header and source; `// wait_for_hbm_vwrite_complete(...)` kept as a possible alternative; the `if (pdc + 1 == dev->num_fetchers)` guard commented out instead of deleted; an #if 0 block of spdlog::debug in a constructor loop; new debug logging under #if 0; a pre-existing warn/check block wrapped in #if 0 (which also removes a check the body does not mention); #if 0 plus commented dump calls after REQUIRE lines in a test. Procedure: flag added lines that are `//` plus code syntax (an identifier followed by `(` or `=` and `;`, or `// if`, `// }`), added `#if 0`, and removed code lines that reappear as comments in the same hunk; ask delete-or-explain, and when the disabled code was a check, report the removed check separately. Ask form: can probably remove the above comments?, can we get rid of this dead code?, if this isn't useful, should get rid of it.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: regex over added lines; fully mechanical.

checks.label: concurrency-race-or-lock-placement
checks.name: Shared state reached from more than one thread without the lock, atomic or wait that protects it
checks.description: What breaks: a race or a torn read. A new parallel weight loader reaches set_hardware_weights on the same PosDevice with no lock on load_weight_q; a per-device mutex array added at the caller in tensor.hpp instead of inside PosDevice or DmaQueue, spanning the busy-wait and missable by future callers; count_complete_gofs() (racy by design) read twice in one block, once in the guard and once in the computation; token_ix_needed narrowed to one mask range so a minibatch no longer waits for a later minibatch writing V entries on the same shared page while scaled_v reads the whole page (Wade's only blocking-severity comment, endorsed via GPT text); a lock_guard held across a whole loop with no comment saying why; only two counters atomic because a FUSE reader runs on another thread; a forwarded Claude item about an undocumented single-writer assumption on process-global relaxed atomics (4800935083). Procedure: for every diff that adds parallel_for, threads or a worker fanout, trace each call inside to its mutable shared object and list the locks on that path; for every added mutex check it lives with the state it guards and covers only the mutating section; for every racy getter count calls per block; for every narrowed readiness predicate (needed, ready, wait, depends) check the consumer's read granularity against the writer's.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for lock placement, double reads of racy getters and narrowed wait predicates (static call-graph reading); confirming an actual race needs runtime evidence.

checks.label: state-written-from-two-sites-or-never-reset
checks.name: One logical record, flag set or lifecycle step is owned by two sites, or by none
checks.description: What breaks: half-filled or stale state. forwards/wall_cycles written by full_scheduler while token_jobs/fpga_queries come from model::run_forward, so another caller of state.forward leaves the record inconsistent; gof_on_save_k/v called unconditionally while gof_configure is gated by a model-shape condition; clear_kv_complete() added with a comment 'called between forward passes' and no caller, so completion flags never clear; an inline definition replaced by an extern declaration with no definition anywhere in the PR; per-worker rows sized by the pool (27) but indexed by attention-worker index (20) so a row mixes threads across forwards; a forward class decided per forward so under continuous batching most decode attention lands in prompt_or_mixed. Procedure: for every struct or counter set the diff writes, list every writer and check one function owns the record; for every gated subsystem list all calls into it and compare their guards with the configure call's guard; for every added reset/clear function require a caller at the lifecycle point its comment names; for every removed definition find the new one; for every table keyed by an index, check the index maps to the same thread/core in every forward and that the production batching puts the common case in the bucket a reader expects. Design concerns are posed as a question with two alternatives.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for writer enumeration, gate comparison and missing callers; the continuous-batching granularity question (4125033664) needs domain knowledge of rinzler batching.

checks.label: code-comment-carries-no-lasting-fact
checks.name: A code comment cites review rounds, tracker ids, the feature that added it, or restates the identifier
checks.description: What breaks: a reader in two years learns nothing technical. 'PR 4596 review round 4, comment W3' in a production header and in a test (Wade: scrub please, there are more); 'Story 2814' in Note [GOF staging eviction]; a three-line comment tying a general-purpose TRACE_EVENT to the feature Note; a 13-line Note [Fixed KV-head slot geometry] for a plain stride bug fix ('not like we are defining some fancy algorithm'); a trailing comment that begins by repeating the member name. Procedure: grep added comment lines for PR #, review, round, comment W<n>/R<n>-M<n>, Story, ticket, JIRA, reviewer names; flag added Note blocks whose content narrates a fix rather than an invariant other code will cite; flag comments that attribute a general statement to the PR's feature; flag comments that start with the declared identifier. Check 9 applies the same reader test to the PR body; this applies it to code comments and Notes (the positron-code-review skill already covers the review-narration part).
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: regex over added comment lines plus a length/content test for new Note blocks.

checks.label: declaration-placement-and-file-organization
checks.name: A declaration, constant block, include or growing function sits where a reader will not look for it
checks.description: What breaks: findability. constexpr constants buried mid-file in hwattention.hpp (move to top, then conceded to config.hpp); pos_driver_register_fuse_stats declared in alloc.hpp (the HBM allocator header) though unrelated to memory alloc; float error helpers in bf16.hpp; "spdlog/spdlog.h" with quotes and apart from the file's <spdlog/fmt/fmt.h>; hw_prepare already several hundred lines and both branches growing (extract helpers, next iteration fine); debug dump functions cluttering the main hardware-attention header (own hwattention_debug module). Procedure: for added namespace-scope constants check they precede the first function/struct or live in the config header; for each added declaration compare the header's topic with the declaration's subsystem; for each added third-party include match the file's bracket style and grouping; for a function the diff grows past a few hundred lines along parallel branches suggest named helpers; for debug helpers in a production header suggest a sibling module. All nits; several explicitly deferred to a later iteration.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: file-position and include-style checks are mechanical; header-topic mismatch needs reading the header comment.

checks.label: silent-behavior-change-in-refactor
checks.name: A hunk changes behavior while presenting as a refactor, cleanup or one-character edit
checks.description: What breaks: a latent bug fix or a regression that no sentence announces. tok_ix switched from .i to token_positions[] with no comment (were we grabbing the wrong token-id all this time?); the NaN/inf special case dropped when the comparison moved into comberr, so hardware-vs-software comparison can produce a false pass; `!= 0` to `!= 1` inverting TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON against its documented meaning; a test swapping DmaQueue::acquire for dev->bypass_read_q with no note; usleep(10) commented out, turning a 10 ms wait into a tight spin. Procedure: for every hunk that replaces one expression with another of the same type, name an input where they differ and check the body states it; for every removed isnan/isfinite/isinf line, trace whether the helper's result still reaches the mismatch branch for NaN; for every changed comparison sense or default resolution, compare with the comment above it and the commit message; for every removed sleep, wait, assert or lock (including one turned into a comment) ask whether it was on purpose. Ask form: was this intentional?, were we just getting lucky so far?, don't we still need to consider nan / inf values?
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: detect same-type expression swaps, removed special-value lines, flipped comparisons and commented-out waits; naming the differing input needs reading the data structures.

checks.label: tests-run-before-merge
checks.name: No evidence that a test exercising the changed path ran at this head, or no test exists for a new primitive
checks.description: What breaks: the approval rests on reading alone. A new multi-producer ring (minfifo) with no test file (ordering, wrap-around); multi-command changes under #ifdef FWD_HW_RESULTS with no statement that the other build was tried; timeout and sentinel changes with a test plan listing only clang-format; a shared_ptr shard pushed onto two edges, so Wade asks whether multi-user runs were done; and his own practice of running the suite on the branch and pasting the ctest summary before approving (4131374395). Procedure: for every new reusable primitive under h/ and src/ require a file under t/ that names it; for every changed region inside #ifdef X with an #else or #ifndef twin, require a body sentence that the opposite build was run; when the body's test plan is static only and the diff touches production constants or hardware-facing code, ask for a representative UT run; when a bot raises a high-severity path finding, ask for the run that exercises that path. Check 3 asks whether an assertion executes on the lane; this widens to whether any run happened at all. Ask form: Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs; did you sanity test that?
checks.agent_feasibility: partial: the static part (new primitive without a t/ file, ifdef twin untested, static-only test plan) is mechanical; the run itself needs a machine with the hardware labels CI cannot run.

checks.label: unrelated-or-unexplained-hunk
checks.name: A hunk, file change or ported snapshot that no body sentence or source branch accounts for
checks.description: What breaks: content enters main that nobody reviewed on purpose. stats/.gitkeep deleted in a one-file gof.cpp fix; a 'DO NOT RENAME as packaging depends on these' comment removed in a PR about something else; `volatile` added to 19 dma_qcsr_t members in a merge PR though neither main nor hwattention_sync has it; h/tron/gof.hpp copied from hwattention_sync at an older revision than the branch head; -mavx/-mfma flags added to the pos library with no explanation of why it built before. Procedure (check 10 plus three triggers it currently excludes): also fire on deleted or added files absent from the body and commit subjects, on removed comment lines whose text names an external consumer (packaging, parsed by, DO NOT RENAME), on files the body says are ported/extracted/copied from a branch (diff them against that branch's head), and on added build flags (ask which symbol failed without them). Ask form: was this intentional?, where is this coming from?, this is an old version, be sure you are rebased to latest.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: file-list vs body diff, removed-comment keyword scan, and a diff against the named source branch are mechanical; the build-flag provenance (2670498736) needs a build.

checks.label: hot-path-avoidable-work
checks.name: Per-call allocation, zeroing, sorting, repeated gathers or unconditional eviction added on a per-token or per-layer path
checks.description: What breaks: throughput. xfer_gofs runs about 4608 times per 4096-token prefill and adds a 128 KiB memset the loops overwrite, six heap vectors where the singleton sibling uses stack arrays, a std::sort emission order makes unnecessary, and a piece-major gather calling v_head_fn 32x more; drain helpers construct and reserve a vector before the empty check inside a spin loop; a TRON_ASSERT re-evaluates 8 std::function calls the caller already asserted; ns_to_cycles paid on every entry before the `0 == wait_cycles` indefinite-wait branch; free_staging_if_idle releases and rebuilds the same GOF buffers with no hysteresis. Procedure: identify functions on prefill/decode/spin paths (callers from token or layer loops); in added lines list heap containers, whole-buffer fills, sorts, nested gathers, asserts duplicating the caller's, and computations before a branch that does not need them; compare with the singleton sibling on the same path; for added frees on a counter reaching zero ask what steady-state pattern re-pays the rebuild. Wade says 'I'm always concerned with performance' and pastes Claude-worded summaries of his concern (4674512577, 5498556672).
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for the static pattern scan and sibling comparison; sizing the cost (how often the path runs, bytes zeroed) needs call-frequency knowledge or a trace.

checks.label: test-name-tag-output-conventions
checks.name: A test's name, tag, log output or file artifacts break the file's convention or state the opposite of its assertions
checks.description: What breaks: the test misleads or pollutes. SECTION still named 'append_v preserves poison' while it asserts the poison is zeroed (ex 5); a TEST_CASE tagged '[hwattention][pos]' where every sibling carries one tag equal to its name; a mismatch count printed unconditionally where siblings print only when nonzero; a replay test writing /tmp/*.json and for_agent/*.json and reading them back with no cleanup, so a stale file can pass as a current result. Procedure: run check 5 on names; compare each new TEST_CASE's tag list with the file's pattern; compare unconditional spdlog::info of a result with the sibling units' guards; list ofstream/fopen paths and check for delete-or-unique-name before the read-back. Ask form: Nit: the section is still named ...; should be consistent?; does this test clean up any existing artifacts it previously generated?
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: all four are static comparisons within the test file.

checks.label: observability-for-new-path
checks.name: New state or a new path lands without a way to see it at runtime
checks.description: What breaks: an operator cannot inspect or measure the feature. New PosDevice fields (prev_cmd_kind, reuse counters) not added to the existing debug_string dump; a new allocator with no TRACE_EVENTs and no 'memory' Perfetto category at all; new Perfetto memory captures described in words with no screenshot; page-share counters as a compile-time option printed at exit where FUSE (the live statistics file interface) with env-var opt-in would allow live and interval reads. Procedure: when a struct with a debug_string/dump/operator<< gains members, check the helper prints them; when a new subsystem or loop-over-all-items path lands with no TRACE_EVENT/TRON_CHECKPOINT, ask whether its cost can be measured; when the PR adds user-visible output, ask for a sample; when a counter is build-time and exit-printed, point to the existing runtime stats layer. Mostly 'no action required' or 'ok approving as-is' questions.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for the debug_string gap and the missing-trace scan; the FUSE alternative needs knowledge of the stats layer (grep attn_stats / set_value / README.stats.md).

checks.label: buffer-lifetime-or-alignment
checks.name: A buffer is freed, reallocated or under-aligned while something still uses it or needs stronger alignment
checks.description: What breaks: a DMA reads freed memory, a reference dangles, or an aligned SIMD store faults. A queued pending_xfer dropped without abandon() releases its buffer while the DMA still reads it (forwarded Claude review, 5498556672, with four sibling items: decode passes with >= 32 users wrongly get the prompt drain budget, hot-path costs, per-shard batch buffers under fanout, two consistency nits); push_back beyond reserve(64) invalidates references into a std::vector held while pushing child frames (std::deque would not); a stack std::array passed to page::get_v() which stores with _mm256_store_si256 (32-byte alignment) with no alignas while the batch sibling has alignas(HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES). Procedure: for every struct that owns a buffer handed to an asynchronous engine, check the destructor or every drop path releases it only after completion; for every function holding a reference into a vector, list grow calls on that vector while the reference is live; for every buffer passed to a callback, find the consumer's intrinsics and compare required alignment with the declared alignment and with the sibling buffer's alignas.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for the static alignment and reference-invalidation reads; proving a fault needs a test that drives the real gather (Wade asked for one).

checks.label: pr-body-and-branch-state
checks.name: PR body claims stale, contradicted or unusable; branch needs squash or rebase
checks.description: What breaks: the reviewer reads a description of a different head. 5420005787 (PR 4557) is the origin of checks 7-11 and 13 in one comment: the required-CI-builds-AMX-off sentence contradicted by cmake-single-platform.yml:355 (check 7), unit-test and token-identity rows citing commits before the merge of main (check 8), assertion-count arithmetic, UTC timestamps and log paths (check 9), AMX tile constants and a t_heap_v2 alignment check that are not typed tensors (check 10), 20 commits with three rewording one Note (check 11), and value-suffixed constant names (check 13); 5371062950 adds the body being stale after several review rounds plus a merge conflict at approval; 4373886636 approves conditional on follow-ups and asks for a rebase. Procedure: run checks 7-11 and 13 at the final head; additionally compare the body's last edit against review-round commits and `gh pr view --json mergeable`; at approval time state whether the body still describes the head. Checks 7-11 are subsumed as written; the stale-after-rounds and mergeability steps extend check 8.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: all steps are gh and git queries plus the existing check procedures.

checks.label: config-value-change-consequences
checks.name: A new or changed capacity, timeout or option is not followed to its runtime consumers, tests and launch wrappers
checks.description: What breaks: the knob exists but its effects are unexamined. max_xfer_time_in_ns cut from 10 s to 100 ms will make the 'DMA XFER saw wait time' log fire far more often, and Wade already saw it with 18446744073709551614 ns on the branch, so he asks what it implies and whether main shows it; inwork_ring_size = 2048 baked into PosDevice instead of a constructor argument (so tests cannot reach wrap-around and full) and with no derivation beside rxinfo_ring_size = 512; a new runtron option --trace-passes not accepted or forwarded by perfetto/tronperf, the wrapper every developer launches through (5106398334 part 2; its part 1 is counted under comment-or-claim-contradicts-code). Procedure: for every changed threshold find the code that changes behavior when a measured value crosses it and any observed values on the branch; for every new sizing constant require a derivation and a way for tests to pick a small size; for every new command-line option, env var or config knob grep bin/, perfetto/ and ci scripts for wrappers that forward sibling options and check the new one is wired.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for the wrapper grep and the constructor-argument testability check; the observed-values question needs a runtime log.

checks.label: workaround-needs-tracking
checks.name: A workaround for an unexplained defect lands with no ticket, or a test makes it permanent with no TODO
checks.description: What breaks: the workaround outlives its reason. A reversed free-list push order described as 'workaround for an unidentified bug' (first DMA hangs when the descriptor ring lands high) with no story id; a TEST_CASE that pins that ordering as a contract (are we enshrining this forever? add a TODO); clear_kv_hbm zeroing KV HBM for NaN garbage that the 'NaN-fixed' bitfile should make unnecessary (harmless to keep, Wade's own to-do). Procedure: grep added comments, commit messages and test headers for workaround, unidentified, unknown bug, hang, hack, TODO without an id; require a ticket id next to the workaround and a TODO in any test that guards it; when the repository or PR mentions a newer hardware/bitfile version, ask whether the workaround can be gated or dropped. Note: Wade asks for tracker ids beside workarounds in code but asks to remove 'Story N' from ordinary Note comments (3350285744); the distinction is whether the comment marks temporary behavior.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes for the keyword scan and the missing-id check; obsolescence after a hardware fix needs domain knowledge.

checks.label: shared-header-owner-signoff
checks.name: A global definition in a widely included header, with no test able to catch a revert, needs the header owner's written acceptance
checks.description: What breaks: ownership. A global operator new[] overload in h/system/memory.hpp whose own Note says no test can catch a regression, arriving via a branch commit of PR 4557 rather than the owner's PR 4698; Wade asks for bgamari's explicit sign-off. Procedure: check 12 as written (global-namespace additions in h/system, h/pos, h/common, h/tron/hardware; unobserved-guarantee wording; includer counts; origin classification; owner comment classification).
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: the existing procedure covers it; the sign-off itself is a question to post, not something the agent obtains.

style_observations: Questions, not orders: 122 of 267 texts contain a question mark (computed over corpus.json); 18 end a clause with 'right?' and 10 ask whether something was 'intention(al)'. Typical openers: 'why ...?', 'can we ...?', 'should we just assert this?', 'was this intentional?', 'still need this log?'.

Suggestion blocks for anything with a one-line fix: 43 texts contain a ```suggestion block (computed). Every typo, type change, macro swap and comment rewording comes as a suggestion block, often followed by '... right?' or 'and similarly elsewhere'.

Severity words are explicit and mild: 'nit' in 10 texts (CONTEXT counts 13 with a looser pattern), 'pedantic' 5, 'IMO/IMHO' 10, 'probably a next iteration/enhancement effort' or 'could be a follow-up' several times. One comment in 273 rows is blocking-severity by hand count (3970590653, V readiness race). 'LGTM' appears 0 times; 'squash' once (5420005787); 'rebase' twice.
Tone markers: ellipses in 94 texts, smileys or 'lol' in 31 (computed). Texts are short: median 128 characters, p90 533, max 2691 (computed). The long ones are forwarded agent reviews.

style_observations: Volume and verdicts (corpus.json, counted): 334 reviews = 100 APPROVED, 234 COMMENTED, 0 CHANGES_REQUESTED. Only 15 review bodies carry text; 4 of those are 40 characters or shorter ('looks good to me'). 0 texts say 'LGTM'; 6 contain 'approve'. Two approvals are conditional in words: 'Approved, assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments. Also needs rebased.' (4373886636) and 'Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs' (4265644124). Approval with a pasted agent-review list as optional follow-ups: 4800935083, 5498556672.

Question form dominates: 122 of 269 texts contain '?'. Of the 239 review rows (273 minus 34 non-review), form = question 93, statement 61, suggestion_block 45, ask 30. He states his reading and asks for confirmation: 19 texts end a claim with 'right?'; 10 ask whether a change was 'intentional' ('leaving enabled intentionally?', 'was this intentional?'); 4 open with 'I assume'; 11 'I think'; 10 'IMO/IMHO'.

Tone markers: 136 of 269 texts start in lowercase, 71 in uppercase (the rest start with a code fence or quote). 96 use '...' ellipses. 24 contain an emoticon (';p', ';)', ':)'), 5 'lol', 5 'pedantic' ('kinda pedantic, but', 'I know this is pedantic... but'), 13 'nit'. 13 texts @-mention the author or another reviewer by handle.

Suggestion blocks: 43 texts carry a ```suggestion block. 17 of the 20 typo rows (H1) are suggestion blocks; the rest are naming (2982403509, 2842854014, 2897235803), stale comments (3405930260, 3437533506, 3120684367), type widening (3437522787 and siblings) and small code edits (3029339639, 3350031805, 3350285744). A suggestion block often ends with '... right?' or a question.

Second instance of a pattern gets a pointer, not a repeat: 6 texts say 'same here', 'ditto' or 'same comment as <link>' (2789796269, 2915281835, 3102603313, 3405974281, 3778058064, 2897211589); 'and this?' twice (2737956124, 2737956568).
